title: Cache invalidation and TTLs

kcs.statement: A fixed TTL limits how long an entry stays in the cache: at most one TTL after it was inserted or last refreshed. It bounds how far the value lags behind source writes only if the value was current when it was cached. A read from a stale replica, or a slow read whose result is written to the cache after a newer write, can break that assumption.
Explicit invalidation removes or updates the cache entry when the source data changes; keeping a TTL as well bounds staleness when an invalidation message is lost.
On a write it is safer to delete the cache key than to set the new value, because two concurrent writers can update the cache in the opposite order from the database and leave a stale value.
